chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, every Imam has a covenant upon the necks of his awliyāʾ and his Shiʿah, and indeed part of complete faithfulness to the covenant is the visitation of their graves. So whoever visits them out of desire for visiting them and in affirmation of that which they encouraged toward, their Imams will be their intercessors on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِهِ: His devoted followers and loyal adherents.
key_terms.إِمَامٍ: An Imam, the divinely appointed leader whose right and covenant are recognized by the believers.
key_terms.زِيَارَةَ: Visitation, especially the devotional visiting of sacred graves.
key_terms.شُفَعَاءَهُمْ: Their intercessors, those who will plead on their behalf before Allah.
key_terms.شِيعَتِهِ: His Shiʿah, those who follow and uphold his authority.
key_terms.عَهْدًا: A binding covenant or pledge of loyalty and obligation.
key_terms.يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ: The Day of Resurrection, when people are raised and judged.
key_terms.ٱلْوَفَاءِ: Faithful fulfillment and complete loyalty to an obligation.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of visiting the graves of the Imams in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the followers of each Imam bear a covenant of loyalty and devotion toward him. Among the complete fulfillment of that covenant is visiting the graves of the Imams, and such visitation—when done out of sincere longing and true affirmation—becomes a cause for the Imams’ intercession on the Day of Judgment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3160 - Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' narrated from Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as) who said:

"Indeed, every Imam has a covenant upon the necks of their followers and Shia, and part of fulfilling this covenant completely is visiting their graves. Whoever visits them out of a desire for their visitation and in affirmation of what they have invited towards, their Imams will be their intercessors on the Day of Judgment."
